items.title: 67260_Freddie Moore oral history interview
items.q: So I had to get somebody to read the stocks. So I got hold of a fellow named Happy Caldwell, a tenor player.

ctx.x: They were cheap in that time.

And Bechet, it was (?), he couldn't read the stocks. He could play all right, but he just couldn't read them stocks. He never wanted to know it. That's the way it is. So I had to get somebody to read the stocks. So I got hold of a fellow named Happy Caldwell, a tenor player. He'd been at (?) for a while. But I was down there, I guess, about three or four years, I think, or something...

So in order to read the stocks... But of course, Bechet, you worked on and off with him in this immediate period after the Second World War. You recorded with him and Art Hodes in '45, and a few years later you were with him at Jimmy Ryan's -- in '47 you played with him, with Sidney Bechet. Did he have his tailor shop here in Harlem at the time?
